root_cause: OlmoeForCausalLM is absent from both of TRT-LLM 0.21.0's model registries: the torch backend MODEL_CLASS_MAPPING (26 architectures) and the TRT engine path (26 models). Qwen3MoeForCausalLM is present in both, which is why Qwen3-30B-A3B does have a TRT-LLM baseline. No configuration can register a model the release does not implement.

transformers bug, not a harness setting. generation/utils.py:664 calls the model's _prepare_4d_causal_attention_mask_with_cache_position without a device argument, but models/olmoe/modeling_olmoe.py:924 still declares device as required. OLMoE is the only one of these models that has not been migrated to the new general mask API: qwen3_moe, qwen3, llama and mixtral contain zero occurrences of the helper and therefore take the new path. Reproduced in 12 lines of pure transformers with a 2-layer random OLMoE: cache_implementation=static raises the identical TypeError, dynamic succeeds.

Two wrapper-level over-allocations, neither in MPK. (1) The wrapper copied MPK's demo CLI defaults (--page-size 4096 --max-num-pages 16 = 65536 KV token slots) while the R16 protocol needs 64+1024=1088 per request; persistent_kernel.cuh draws ceil((step+new)/page_size) pages per request from one queue of MPK_MAX_NUM_PAGES, so B1 needs 1 page, not 16 (8.00 -> 0.50 GiB of KV). (2) The binding cause: the wrapper ran --batch all, rebuilding a PersistentKernel for each of 10 (batch, output length) cells in one process, and finalize_persistent_kernel() frees the runtime's task/event/queue state but not the fused weight buffers the generated launcher cudaMallocs (per layer q/k/v into one qkv and gate/up into one gatedup, originals kept). Those are outside the torch caching allocator and never returned.
evidence: verified: mem_get_info around each build measures 9.53 GiB retained per kernel build for this model (static sum of the launcher's cudaMalloc sizes in test_rank0.cu: 8.50 GiB over 78 sites, 224 MiB per layer gatedup + 40 MiB per layer qkv). R4 log0.txt OOMs at B8 round 0 with '78.74 GiB in use, 26.95 GiB allocated by PyTorch' = 51.8 GiB non-PyTorch against 6 prior builds x 8.50 GiB = 51.0 GiB predicted (1.6% apart). Fix: one process per (batch, output length) cell plus a derived page budget; the wrapper now refuses a build whose retained-byte requirement exceeds free memory instead of OOMing inside MPK.

root_cause: Same two causes, reached earlier because the 61 GB expert weights leave only ~12 GiB of headroom: R4 died in the second build of the first cell (B1 kernel_N1024) at 'CUDA error at test.cu:1060: out of memory', the per-layer fused qkv cudaMalloc of layer 33 of 48. A third contributor is specific to this model: MPK allocates with cudaMalloc, which cannot draw on the torch caching allocator's freed blocks, and the wrapper's expert stacking (torch.stack of 128 experts per layer, then del layer.mlp.experts) churns ~57 GiB through that cache, so the driver saw almost nothing free when MPK's launcher started.
evidence: verified: launcher retains 0.94 GiB per build (static sum over 69 cudaMalloc sites in test_rank0.cu, 20 MiB fused qkv x 48 layers dominant); KV pool 6.00 -> 0.38 GiB at B1 with the derived budget. Fix adds torch.cuda.empty_cache() after the expert stacking and after each finalize so the freed blocks return to the driver. MPK itself is unmodified.

root_cause: MPK 63af900 reaches a model by one of two independent paths and neither covers this architecture. (a) The demos, which this wrapper replicates, exist only for Qwen3ForCausalLM (demo/qwen3/demo_hopper.py), Qwen3MoeForCausalLM (demo/qwen3/demo_30B_A3B_hopper.py) and LlamaForCausalLM (demo/llama3/demo.py). (b) mirage.mpk.model_registry, used by MPK's own serving engine rather than the demos, registers deepseek-v3, Glm4Moe, gpt_oss, Inkling and Qwen3 (dense) only. Note the registry covers none of the three demo architectures either, so the registry refusal alone is not the reason a model is out of reach -- the absence of a demo is.
evidence: verified: get_builder() raises 'Unknown builder' for OlmoeForCausalLM, MistralForCausalLM, Qwen3MoeForCausalLM and LlamaForCausalLM alike against the registered list above; the DEMOS table in mpk_baseline.py is the operative support set. Building a task graph for a new architecture means writing an MPK demo, which would be new MPK work, not a configuration change.
